'''Izumo Furune''' (出雲振根, [[dates of birth and death unknown]]) was a local noble from the [[Kofun period]] mentioned in the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}. There is no reference to him in the {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}}, but a similar account is given in which {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|倭建命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ヤマトタケル|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q461258}} defeated {{ill|Izumo Takeru|ja|出雲建|qid=Q28688775}}.

== Overview ==
According to the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}, Emperor {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|qid=Q333530|lt=Sujin}} decreed to his retainers, "I wish to see the divine treasures said to have been brought from heaven by {{ill|Takehi-Nateru|fr|Takehi-Nateru|ja|建比良鳥命|zh|建比良鳥命|qid=Q11065428}}, also called Takehinatori or Amenohinatori. These treasures are stored in the shrine of Izumo Ōkami ({{ill|Kumano Taisha|ja|熊野大社|simple|Kumano Taisha|zh|熊野大社|qid=Q11568887|lt=Kumano Taisha}} or {{ill|Izumo-taisha|ja|杵築神|lt=Izumo Taisha}})." To fulfill this wish, a warrior named {{ill|Take Morosumi|ja|矢田部造武諸隅}} (also recorded as Ōmorosumi), an ancestor of the Yatabe clan, was dispatched to present the treasures.

At that time, the treasures were managed by {{ill|Izumo Furune|ja|出雲振根}}, an ancestor of the Izumo clan, but he was away in {{ill|Tsukushi Province|en|Tsukushi Province|qid=Q1206461|lt=Tsukushi Province}}. In his absence, his brother {{ill|Iiirine|ja|飯入根|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iiinone|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q55533680}}, acting independently, accepted the imperial command and sent the treasures to the court with his brother {{ill|Umashikara Hisa|ja|甘美韓日狭}} and son {{ill|Ukazukunu|ja|鸕濡渟}}.

Upon his return from Tsukushi, Furune learned of this and reproached his brother:

*"You should have waited a few days. Why did you so easily hand over the divine treasures?"*

Unable to let go of his resentment, Furune harbored a grudge for years and eventually decided to kill his brother. He deceived Iiinone by saying:

*"Lately, reeds have grown thick around the pools of Stopoya (modern-day {{ill|Izumo, Shimane|ar|إزومو (شيمانه)|arz|ازومو|azb|ایزومو|bar|Izumo (Shimane)|be|Ідзума (горад)|ca|Izumo|ce|Идзумо (гӀала)|ceb|Izumo|cs|Izumo (Šimane)|de|Izumo (Shimane)|el|Ιζούμο (Σιμάνε)|eo|Izumo (Ŝimane)|es|Izumo (Shimane)|et|Izumo|eu|Izumo (Shimane)|fa|ایزومو|fi|Izumo|fr|Izumo (Shimane)|gl|Izumo|id|Izumo, Shimane|it|Izumo|ja|出雲市|ko|이즈모시|mg|Izumo|nl|Izumo|no|Izumo (Shimane)|pl|Izumo (miasto)|pt|Izumo (Shimane)|ro|Izumo|ru|Идзумо (город)|sh|Izumo|simple|Izumo, Shimane|sr|Изумо|sv|Izumo|tg|Изумо|th|อิซูโมะ|tl|Isumo, Shimane|tr|Izumo (şehir)|tt|Идзумо (шәһәр)|uk|Ідзумо (Сімане)|ur|ایزومو، شیمانے|uz|Izumo|vi|Izumo, Shimane|war|Izumo, Shimane|zh|出雲市|zh_classical|出雲市|zh_min_nan|Izumo-chhī|zh_yue|出雲|qid=Q825166|lt=Izumo City}}, Shimane Prefecture). Let’s go and see them together."*

At the poolside, Furune said:

*"The water is so clear. Why don’t we bathe together?"*

Furune then tricked his brother by swapping his sword with a wooden replica he had prepared earlier. As Iiinone emerged from the water, Furune killed him with the real sword.

This scene was immortalized in a waka:

{{quotation|Yagumo rises, proud warrior of Izumo, with a blade bound in black ivy, alas, no true blade to be found.}}

Iiinone's brother and son reported the details to the imperial court. As a result, Emperor Sujin dispatched generals {{ill|Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto|fr|Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto|ja|吉備津彦命|zh|吉備津彥命|qid=Q65318}} and {{ill|Take Nunokawa Wake no Mikoto|ja|武渟川別|zh|武渟川别|qid=Q11546050}} to kill Furune.

Subsequently, the Izumo clan refrained from worshiping Izumo Ōkami until a woman named {{ill|hikatobe|ja|氷香戸辺|qid=Q55533080}} from {{ill|Tanba Province|cs|Tanba (provincie)|de|Provinz Tamba|es|Provincia de Tanba|fa|ولایت تانبا|fr|Province de Tanba|gl|Provincia de Tanba|id|Provinsi Tamba|it|Tanba (provincia)|ja|丹波国|ko|단바국|lt|Tambos žemė|nl|Tamba (provincie)|pt|Província de Tanba|ru|Тамба (провинция)|simple|Tamba Province|sk|Tanba (provincia)|sr|Провинција Тамба|tr|Tamba (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Тамба|zh|丹波國|zh_min_nan|Tanba-kok|qid=Q954511|lt=Tanba Province}}, [[Hikami District]], sang a song taught to her child. This led the emperor to reinstate the worship of Izumo Ōkami with mirrors.<ref>Nihon Shoki, Emperor Sujin's 60th year, 7th month, 14th day.</ref>

Eight years later, Emperor Sujin passed away.

According to the Nihon Shoki, 34 years later, in the 26th year of Emperor {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|qid=Q314850|lt=Suinin}}, the imperial court sent the high-Ranking official {{ill|Mononobe no Tokone|ja|物部十千根|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe no Tōchine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q24885356}} to inspect the divine treasures in Izumo.<ref>Nihon Shoki, Emperor Suinin's 26th year, 8th month, 3rd day.</ref>

== Analysis ==
The above story closely resembles the tactics employed by {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ヤマトタケル|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q461258}} in defeating Izumo Takeru during Emperor {{ill|Emperor Keikō|en|Emperor Keikō|qid=Q329723|lt=Keikō}}'s reign, suggesting a conflation of traditions. Notably, the Nihon Shoki's account of Yamato Takeru does not mention any visit to Izumo.

Many theories identify the "Izumo Ōkami" referenced in the treasure-offering episode with {{ill|Izumo-taisha|ja|杵築大社|lt=Izumo Taisha}}, but since the treasures were associated with the ancestors of the Izumo clan, there is also a possibility of {{ill|Kumano Taisha|ja|熊野大社|simple|Kumano Taisha|zh|熊野大社|qid=Q11568887|lt=Kumano Taisha}} in {{ill|Ou district|ja|意宇郡|zh|意宇郡|qid=Q11073594}}. Scholars such as {{ill|Mitsusada Inoue|ja|井上光貞|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mitsusada Inoue|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11372857}} have argued that the narrative reflects a rivalry between eastern Izumo groups worshiping Kumano Taisha and western Izumo groups worshiping Izumo Taisha.<ref>Nihon Shoki (Vol. 1), Iwanami Shoten, 1994, p. 299.</ref>
